messages:
jamal: Heads-up: we saw a sudden p50 jump on serving-prod around 18:05 UTC and the KV prefix hit-rate collapsed from ~92% to 12% in <3m. Likely correlated with the kernel-selector rollout yesterday. :eyes:

alex: on it. which rollout specifically? kernel-selector_v2 or the quantize rollout?

jamal: kernel-selector_v2 was toggled to aggressive_matmul across canaries at 17:50, and q8_0 quant profile was enabled for a subset of tenants at 17:57. timing matches the onset.

mira: I pulled perf histograms. p50 went 42ms -> 240ms, p95 180ms -> 1.1s. throughput dropped ~30% on the affected shards.

ravi: logs show rapid prefix_eviction spikes around 18:04. snippet from runtime log: ``[18:04:12] eviction: prefix_shard=12 keys=192 evicted=178 reason=ttl_or_pressure`` then repeated every few seconds.

jamal: exact eviction log copied here: 
```
[18:04:12] cache_evict INFO tenant=acme shard=12 prefix=usr:embed:* evicted=178 active_keys=14 total_capacity=2048
[18:04:13] cache_evict INFO tenant=acme shard=12 prefix=usr:embed:* evicted=200 active_keys=6
```

mira: that looks like cache poisoning via high-cardinality prefixes from a noisy tenant. But why now after kernel change?

alex: theory: aggressive_matmul changed tokenization/seq packing in some model variants which altered prefix key formation (e.g., a missing normalization step), causing many near-unique prefixes and bypassing prefix aggregation -> explosion in prefix cardinality.

sylvia: can we reproduce with a local canary? I can run a small load test with a tenant fixture and the same kernel selection + q8 profile.

jamal: yes please. add logging to show prefix keys generated (hash prefix first 8 chars) and sampling of inputs. keep at low qps to avoid causing prod noise.

ravi: started a perf recording on the affected node: `curl http://node-12:6060/debug/pprof/profile?seconds=30 > p.prof`. also enabled flame graphs.

infra-bot: deploy-notification: rolled kernel-selector_v2=aggressive_matmul to canaries at 2025-11-06T17:50:12Z by alex.

mira: from pprof sample: majority of CPU time in `kv::lookup_prefix` and `string::normalize_for_prefix` which indicates prefix normalization is now costly or called more frequently. flamegraph shows repeated calls from model tokenization path.

alex: I grepped the recent commit: the kernel selector change included a tiny refactor that accidentally reordered a normalization call. pushing a revert patch now: `git revert 3a9f7c2` and will canary revert on one shard.

jamal: good. in parallel, can we raise `kv.prefix_eviction_threshold` by 5x as a short mitigation to avoid immediate collapse? that buys time for rollback.

ravi: patch applied to config on shard-12; threshold increased from 0.2 -> 1.0. hit-rate crawled back to ~68% over 2m, latency improving.

sylvia: local canary with the exact kernel + q8 reproduced the prefix cardinality spike. sample inputs attached to the canary log show tokenization differences (extra leading space tokens).

mira: verdict: regressions caused by reorder in kernel selection path that skipped a trimming step before prefix generation; combined with q8 quant changes producing slightly different token boundaries -> high cardinality prefixes -> eviction spiral -> latency/throughput degradation.

alex: next actions: revert kernel-selector commit from canaries -> prod, add unit test for prefix normalization idempotence, add integration test with kernel selection permutations, and adjust release checklist to include prefix-hit sanity checks.

jamal: filed incident ticket INC-2025-542 and added checklist items. thanks all. :thumbsup:

infra-bot: incident created: INC-2025-542 (kv-prefix-hit-collapse) assigned to eng-runtime oncall.

sylvia: follow-up: I'll open a small PR to add a lightweight metric `prefix_cardinality_99` and a gating alert if it exceeds 5k for a shard for >1m.

jamal: please CC ops and oncall. we should also run a backfill to check historical correlation with previous kernel rollouts.
